title: the measure48 host form's stop-line test under CI load: its gates read the wall clock
note: basis 'shown' means shown by reading the code and by 30 runs of the test beside 8 busy processes on 4 cores in a session container, at master and at the card's head; the CI failure itself was read from its log, not rerun.

findings.claim: the stop-line test of tests/unit/test_measure48_host_h67.py ran the host form on the real clock with a second counted as 150 and the line at 64 min: stage 4's gate (high 1.05 h) had 60 scaled seconds, 0.4 s of wall time, from the start of the steps, and the ladder's (stage 6, high 0.80 h) 6.4 s; on a loaded machine either was used up, a stage was not started and the line never reached the hang (CI job 138687984359; 7 of 30 runs here)

the product's rule is not the fault: tools/measure48-host.sh and tools/measure48-vm.sh are unchanged; the test now runs them on a stand-in clock (a date on the rig's PATH) that stands still until the hanging measure has started and is then moved past the line, so no gate depends on wall time
